source: May et al. (2021), AJ 162, 158, 'Spitzer Phase-curve Observations and Circulation Models of the Inflated Ultrahot Jupiter WASP-76b' (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ac0e30; arXiv:2107.03349). Spitzer IRAC 3.6 um phase curves wa076bo11 (3-5 May 2017) and wa076bo12 (21-23 April 2018), program 13038, fitted jointly with one set of phase parameters. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: section 3.2 and appendix Table 4 (table:all_params), columns wa076bo11 and wa076bo12, which print the same map.

model.description: SPIDERMAN spherical harmonics, second order: 'we only consider the two terms that create a dipole centered at a latitude and longitude of zero degrees, and use SPIDERMAN's longitude offset parameter' (section 2.2). Table 4 lists, for the joint 3.6 um fit, sph0 (Y00) and sph3 (Y11); the two other second-order terms are zero. Its note: 'We use the lon0/lat0 options in spiderman'.

spiderman.lo0Reading: Table 4 prints lo0 = 0.68 [deg]; SPIDERMAN takes radians, so the fit passed 0.68 degrees = 0.011868 rad, read the same way as the 4.5 um record (phase-curve.json). In spiderman-package 1.0.3 the lo0 slot moves the dipole in latitude, not longitude (see the WASP-76b README).

dilution.where: section 2.3, dilution factor at 3.6 um for the companion WASP-76 B

daysideK.where: section 3.2, disk-integrated day side brightness temperature (Kurucz stellar model)

nightsideK.where: section 3.2, disk-integrated night side brightness temperature

semiAmplitude.where: section 3.2; the paper does not say whether this is half the peak-to-peak or whether it is dilution corrected
